options.text: A test that passes and fails without any change to the code

questions.explanation: Flaky tests are non-deterministic — they depend on some uncontrolled input, so results vary between identical runs.

questions.prompt: Why is automatic retry-until-green a poor response to flakiness?

options.text: It makes tests run slower only
It masks the non-determinism and any real intermittent bug instead of removing the cause

questions.explanation: Retries hide the underlying cause (and possibly a real race), so the bug still ships while CI looks green and trust erodes.

questions.prompt: Which are common causes of flaky tests? Select all that apply.

options.text: Reliance on real time, dates, or time zones

questions.explanation: Shared state, real time, and unseeded randomness are classic non-determinism sources; asserting a return value is just normal testing.

questions.prompt: Temporarily moving a stubbornly flaky test out of the blocking suite while you fix it is called ____.
questions.explanation: Quarantine protects CI's trustworthiness as a stopgap; it is not a fix, and you never skip/delete a test just to go green.

questions.prompt: Match each flakiness cause to its real fix.

pairs.right: Fake the dependency; no real I/O

questions.explanation: Each cause has a determinism-restoring fix — isolate state, control time, seed RNG, and remove real I/O.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to diagnose and address a flaky test.

items.text: Identify the uncontrolled input (state, time, randomness, I/O)
Remove the cause; quarantine only if a fix takes time

questions.explanation: Reproduce, find the root cause, then fix it — with quarantine as a temporary measure, never retries as the answer.
